>Note that it says during a referendum. This means he can use his power
>during bloodhunts. That is huge! Here come that Pot/For Nossie Marching
>Army of Amarath.

Hugest in Camarilla Edition games, or limited draft, mostly.

There are a lot of decks out there that still don't use Princes. Weenie
Legacy of Pander can still be viable - 6 to 8 votes from your weenies
isn't bad at all. Independent Free States Rants decks don't die -
though a few may be including a useful cross-over prince. As some have
pointed out, Ellison (not a prince) might be a useful cross-over vamp.
The Ventrue lose out slightly, but they've gained with Creepshow Casino
and the Daughters of Cacophony combo reasonably well with them.

I'd also point out that - similarly - Gustav Mallenhous was going to be
a huge, broken, end-of-the-world (I paraphrase - and exaggerate) boost
for the Ventrue Antitribu, but I've rarely seen him played, let alone
used. (This may be specific. I'd be interested if other people are
having problems with him.)

It will *probably* curtail a little [1/2] Brujah activity (and some of
[2/3], if [3] Brujahs fit with the EuroBrujah, Theo Bell etc.) - which I
don't see as being entirely problematic - the versatility of the current
[1/2] Brujah is rather high. They can bleed, they can bleed at stealth
(Carthage Remembered), they can vote, they can hit out in combat well.
Oh, and the EuroBrujah can bounce. Pretty versatile.

Only, to my mind, the Lasombra can match this versatility - and they're
slightly screwed in a number of ways, relatively - not as good combat
support, limited vote push, large titles etc. Of course, the Lasombra
aren't screwed by Ellison, unless they choose to combo with Marcus Vitel
- which may be good for the right deck.

disipline. To be more specific, you are attempting to chose the vamps
that will go your new "beat the hell out of em" Bruja deck, and are
coming to the final cuts. Given the following list, which would you
choose?

combat deck:
You need to considder both defence as well as offence.

Donal O'Connor <POT DOM CEL> 8
Taura Vaughn <dom PRES POT CEL> 8
Miranda Sanova <aus obf pot PRES CEL> 8

While there is nothing wrong with any one of these three vamps,
unless you are attempting to prove a point, generally Miranda will
not often make the cut. In fact in most cases, she would be probubly
be passed over for a !Bruja rather than include her. Personally I have
never used her in anything other than in Bruja political decks...and
then not that often.

Certainly you could argue that Miranda has an excellent discipline
spread and state that she would fit beautifully when attemptempting to
make up for the Bruja's lack of intercept and stealth, however there
are definatly not enough Bruja with these skills to make them usefull.
I personally wouldn't bother including Behind You's and Enhanced
Senses based on this one vamp.

Instead you might notice that Both Donol and Taura have dom, infact
many other Bruja have dom instead and in addition to traditional pres
in clan. Donal has it at sup and Taura at inf. At this point I would
cut Taura

Could this lead to a theme?

Rather than attempting to keep up with those nasty stealth bleed
decks, make them usefull to you. Get them to bleed your prey for you.
Happy!! Add to this ridiculas bleed and (I could go on and on about
the versitillity of dom) you get the point.

And suddenly EuroBruja is born.

I guess this is a counter point to my own argument as dom is an out of
clan discp, however it takes three vamps from Dark Soverighn's to make
this deck feasible. Additionally Theo usally gets put in this deck. So
perhaps it actually lends some strength and credibillity. You decide.

Of course there are a million counters to this as it is easy to
include multiple skills and splits over many clans (especially post
blood lines) but in my opinion there is a disperity between the
origional Vtes and Jyhad sets vamps versus say the Sabbat clans that
tend to be more highly focused and efficient.

For an example of this we could examine the !Bruja in the same
capacity range. This will fall a little short as there is currently
only one !Bruja with the matching capacity, but Jacko is nothing short
of a killing machine. He works well in just about any pot deck that
breaks things and hurts people. A thousand times over I would chose
Jacko for the above deck over Miranda.

As an aside, how easy is it to build a deck with 12 copies of Lambach
or Lasvernius? I've done both and disgusted my friends with them...
There are tourney winning decks based on at least Lambach that I've
seen on Lasombra's sight. I haven't botherd to search for Lasvernus,
but doing this would not be differcult (especially with the up coming
multirush concept, I shudder to think about the possibillities that
you could do with this beast) perhaps even easy post CamEd.

Another terrific example would be say Alyea, she works just as well in
a Lasombra deck as !Tremere. The examples go on and on, but the
examples of the Cam super characters are a little more lean (imo) even
though there are many more Cam vamps than Sabbat.

I guess this can be attributed to the fact that they use a different
formula for creating the origional Vtes critters and newer vamps, but
this is kind of the point.

Enough rambling, these are entirely opinion on my part, I would be
interested in hearing other's opinions pre and post Cam. This could be
truly interesting.

I see what you mean but I don't usually put a lot of truck in using
the winning decks as an overall gauge of what is about at any given
time. I find that in general, the winning deck at any given tourney is
not indicative of the 'feel' of a tourney. i.e.. a tourney with a lot
of sneaky bleed is not *usually* won by a sneak and bleed deck.

It follows (in my experience at least!) that the amount / type of
other decks at a tourney are a much better measure of the current
trends and form. Obviously this is extremely difficult to quantify but
have a look at the next tourney you are at, its a pretty interesting
observation to make. It really does not take a lot extra of one type
to create a feeling of a 'combat tourney' or a 'vote heavy tourney',
players will obviously have different opinions of the tourney because
of seating, deck type, play styles etc. but in general I reckon you
can see a pattern of non-conformist deck type's winning tourneys.

Anyway I digress.

Hmmmm. Agreed, again I think this could easily be attributed to
players 'trying out' all the new toys as you mention later. I think
the shift in the pattern I mentioned might come 6 mths or a year down
the line, but players will slowly find / realise that no matter how
good the new vamps are they cannot compete with the minion advantage
that weenies provide. A bit of a wild statement but simple facts point
this out to me - 5th *may* no longer be available as a 'staple'
fill-up in a lot of decks that use big vamp powers with multiple
actions or cards that grant action rich (and blood intensive) effects
such as Force of Will. Minion Tap / 5th will no longer be a viable and
competitive option which IMO is one of the main defences that the
larger cap decks have when facing overwhelming numbers.

Then again, playing devil's advocate to my own ramblings leads me to
look at Sabbat and Indies as an opposing case to this argument. The
larger vamps of the Sabbat and a lot of the Independents are being
used very well without such a powerful instant gain card. Why is this?

Thinking back to my own creations, I have always been much more aware
of cumulative card costs and the resultant problems in non-camarilla
decks simply because of the lack of 5th. At present I think the
Camarilla are still *more* powerful (but more importantly have more
access to more powerful effects) than the other sects. If the other
rumours are to be believed, 2nd Trad., Hostile Takeover, Majesty and
ToGP have all had depowering text changes which, whatever your opinion
on the new set is *will* change the game. With Sabbat/SW we saw a much
better balance of vamps, in that Jyhad/VTES was subject to quite a few
miscosted and quite frankly shit high cap vamps. This has slowly led
to more decks being created with the 'good value' Sabbat vamps
(Prisci, stock 7, 8 caps like Meschenka and Gratiano) and more
recently Final Nights and Bloodlines vamps in which all the exciting
new ones were nearly all mid to high cap (and quite rightly so).

Take the example of a powerful Camarilla archetype 'the Ventrue Law
firm' in its various incarnations. The amount of changes that the
library of this deck would go through is worrying. *A lot* of
increased costs would arise from Majesty, 2nd Trad etc. whilst the
potential for blood gain (and subsequently combat survival) would
decrease drastically. These 'classic' archetypes become less appealing
and less powerful as the space needed to counter these negative
effects can only detract from the decks effectiveness. For me, it
follows (stay with me :o) that players will find alternatives to try
and win tourneys with and these will be lower capacity decks of
Camarilla vamps *not* reliant on 5th for blood gain and the same, if
not more decks of the Sabbat and Indie mid caps.

As an aside, I think we will see an increase in disposable vamp decks
of all sorts. I would expect Minion Tap (a few turns of frantic use)
and then Golconda to become a much more prevalent (and potent)
strategy.

To what extent are the winning decks a factor of the metagame, and

previously won?

Part of the reason why I focussed on winning decks is that they
represent most of the information we have about the kinds of decks
that are present at tournaments. The other part of the reason,
however, is that they represent what is succeeding at tournaments,
which in my mind represents the state of the balance of power in
the game.

>Every additional rescue attempt costs a blood and a card from hand (for

Yes, but those cards are fairly easy to cycle and are extremely useful anyway.
From what I've seen, lots of decks don't mind packing in plenty of

>How is this cheesier than Mirror Image, Shadow Body, or misc. BL S:CE+cont

Because unless you draw additional stealth, a single Wake or Forced Awakening
will shut you down. Vampire A takes an action, Vampire B wakes and blocks. If
Vampire A continues the action with Shadow Body or Mirror Image, Vampire B can
just block again (without needing to play any additional cards). Vampire A can
keep playing "S:CE, action continues" but Vampire B can keep blocking without
additional cards. (We can assume for the moment that Vamp A had already used
the card for stealth and Vamp B has a Sport Bike, if you're wondering why Vamp
A doesn't just use the Shadow Body for stealth...).

But with repeated Majesty/Freak Drive, each time you get blocked, you tap the
blocker (or use up the Wake) and then do another action. Unless you're playing
with Animalism and Cat's Guidance, it's going to be virtually impossible for
the other Methusaleh to untap enough times to prevent the action from going
through.

>the would-be blocker tapped unless he woke, but doesn't risk combat,
>either.).

I don't really understand the "my super deck tech is super secret"
attitude. To me, it's much more interesting to spread useful
knowledge as widely as possible; it's more fun to play when my
opponents can learn more from my decks as well as vice versa.

I can understand the desire to obtain some competitive advantage
by springing surprises on people - and that is also fun to do -
but once a deck has won a tournament, it is to my mind time for
it to be in the public domain and available to all. That is, if
a deck of mine has won a tournament once, that's all it needs to
do, from my point of view; if I never play it again in a tournament
that's fine, and if other people do, that's fine too.

(Plus, I find it flattering if people even try playing my decks
in tournaments, let alone beat me with them. :-)

> Me, I don't like to post my TWDs anywhere near GenCon. As a matter of
> fact, last year, before the GenCon final, I was reading Ben's decklist
> from the qualifier. :)

Now, I'll certainly admit that I am very reluctant to play any
of the decks of mine that have been posted in the past year (due
to having won tournaments) at GenCon. And this is largely because
I think people would know what to expect from them and that they
would be substantially less effective because of it. And yes,
this does mean more work for me in coming up with new deck ideas
and developing them to a competitive level. But personally, I
wouldn't have it any other way: more new decks equals more new
fun, and a totally new deck can be a surprise to everybody (except
perhaps the people in your local group that you've been testing
it against) where a "recycled" one will be familiar to at least
some of the people at GenCon (eg the ones you've played it against
in earlier tournaments).

Josh
